# Web Speech APIs

> Some of these APIs (`chrome.tts`) are extension-only; where a rule touches
> MV3 service-worker / content-script mechanics, only the speech-API facet is
> here — the general extension gotcha underneath is not.

## Speech-to-text (`webkitSpeechRecognition` / Web Speech API)

- **The recognizer owns its own microphone capture — you cannot hand it
  `getUserMedia` audio constraints.** `echoCancellation` / `noiseSuppression` /
  `autoGainControl` are `getUserMedia` *microphone* constraints, and the recognizer
  exposes no hook to set them on its internal stream (Chrome applies its default
  echo cancellation there regardless). To *warm* the device with a known processing
  state — and to read back whether echo cancellation actually engaged — run a
  separate preflight `getUserMedia({ audio: {…} })` capture and stop its tracks.
  (`suppressLocalAudioPlayback` /
  `restrictOwnAudio` are `getDisplayMedia` *screen-capture* constraints and have no
  bearing on a mic — don't reach for them here.)
- **Read the whole n-best list, not just alternative `[0]`.** Set
  `maxAlternatives` > 1 and iterate `result[0..length]` for `{ transcript,
  confidence }`; the ranked alternatives are exactly where homophone / near-miss
  recovery lives. (1)
- **`onresult`, `onend`, and `onerror` all fire — settle the cycle exactly once.**
  Guard a `settled` flag: interim results arrive before the final one, a cycle can
  end with no result at all (treat `onend`-without-result as `no-speech`), and an
  error and an end can both arrive. (2)
- **With `interimResults` off, engines omit `isFinal` — treat a result as final
  unless `isFinal === false`.** Don't test `if (result.isFinal)` (it's `undefined`
  on those engines and you'll drop every result); test `result.isFinal !== false`.
- **The classic recognizer streams audio to a cloud service (Google's) — plan for
  it.** A `network` error means "offline / service unreachable", and audio leaves
  the machine. On-device recognition is opt-in and capability-gated: probe
  `SpeechRecognition.available({ langs, processLocally: true }) === 'available'`
  once and cache it, set `recognizer.processLocally = true`, and **never trigger a
  language-pack download** (only `'available'` counts, not `'downloadable'`). When
  the local path is absent, fall back to ordinary cloud recognition unchanged.
- **Contextual biasing (`SpeechRecognitionPhrase` + `recognizer.phrases`) works
  only on the on-device path** — gate it behind that same availability probe and
  apply it best-effort (any failure falls back to un-biased recognition rather than
  breaking the listen cycle). Only bias **closed vocabularies you control**
  (a command lexicon, known labels, a spelling alphabet) with **modest** boosts:
  over-boosting makes the recognizer hear a biased phrase when the user actually
  said a same-sounding free-form utterance.
- **Map the raw Web Speech error names to a small taxonomy** — `not-allowed` /
  `service-not-allowed` → permission-denied, plus `no-speech`, `network`,
  `aborted`, `audio-capture`, else `other`. In particular `aborted` is the
  *self-inflicted* stop (you called `recognizer.abort()`), so the caller should
  ignore it rather than surface it as a failure.
- **A missed endpoint mid-utterance needs a pause watchdog, not just `onend`.**
  If interim hypotheses exist but no final arrives, the engine may have lost the
  endpoint; a timer that fires after a pause discards the half-heard input and
  reopens a fresh cycle (preventing "heart heart" doubles when the user repeats
  themselves). Set the threshold **well above a natural mid-command thinking
  pause** — a tight window (~1.2 s) cuts real commands; a wider one (~1.8 s) keeps
  only the genuine missed-endpoint case.
- **Mic permission is per-origin, and the grant belongs to whatever page the
  recognizer runs in.** In a content script the prompt reads as the *host site*
  asking and the grant persists for that origin. Surface it in a controlled moment:
  preflight `navigator.permissions.query({ name: 'microphone' })`, then a one-time
  `getUserMedia` to raise the prompt. **Retry the capture bare** (`{ audio: true }`)
  if the first constrained call is rejected — a browser balking at the constraint
  *shape* must not be misread as a permission denial; only a second failure is a
  real "denied".

## Text-to-speech (`chrome.tts` / `speechSynthesis`)

- **Prefer `chrome.tts` over `speechSynthesis` — it's immune to page
  autoplay / user-activation gating.** `speechSynthesis` invoked from a content
  script is subject to the host page's autoplay policy and can silently refuse to
  speak; `chrome.tts` (extension-only, needs the `"tts"` permission, usable from the
  service worker) is not. Make `chrome.tts` primary and `speechSynthesis` the
  fallback for non-extension document contexts.
- **`chrome.tts` doesn't exist in a content script — relay speak/cancel to the
  service worker over a port.** Keep the same `speak()`/`cancel()` contract on both
  sides; the in-page port sends `{ speak }` / `{ cancel }` messages and the worker
  drives `chrome.tts`. On port disconnect, resolve every pending `speak()` promise

  finish.

  "no voices".** Resolve the preferred voice on the *first* `speak()` and don't
  cache an empty result: fall back to the default that turn and try to resolve

- **(RULES-3)** Chrome's automatic echo cancellation on the recognizer's own capture is a
  loopback of the *page's* playout, so it attenuates `speechSynthesis` but never sees
  `chrome.tts`, whose audio the OS renders outside the page. That leaves a residual echo no
  capture-layer constraint can reach — which is why the string-match guard against what was
  just spoken is the design rather than a workaround, and why reaching for a constraint
  instead means the guard never gets written. Reaffirm while `chrome.tts` renders outside the
  page's audio graph; retire if the recognizer gains a constraint hook or AEC starts covering
  OS-rendered output.
- **(RULES-4)** The preferred-voice order and the speaking rate were both set once as
  constants in CrosswordChat and both turned out wrong for real users — the failure mode of a
  taste judgment frozen into source. Reaffirm while voice availability and preference remain
  per-machine and per-person; retire if engines converge on a voice good enough that a
  default needs no escape hatch.
- **(check:mic-capture-released)** A `getUserMedia` stream is freed only by stopping its
  tracks: dropping the reference, closing an `AudioContext` or unsetting a `srcObject` frees
  nothing, and both the browser's recording indicator and the OS microphone indicator stay
  lit. On a voice app that is the most alarming possible bug — it looks to the user like the
  app is still listening. File-scoped rather than flow-scoped on purpose: proving a
  particular stream is stopped needs real data-flow analysis, and a check that guesses is
  worse than one asking an honest question. Reaffirm while track-stopping is the only
  release; retire if streams gain deterministic collection.
- **(check:mic-constraints-not-screen-capture)** `suppressLocalAudioPlayback` and
  `restrictOwnAudio` are `getDisplayMedia` screen-capture constraints; `getUserMedia` ignores
  them with no throw, no warning and no `OverconstrainedError`. They are reached for by name
  by someone hunting their app's own TTS leaking back through the mic, so the cost is not the
  dead property but the application-level echo guard (RULES-3) that never gets written.
  Reaffirm while the constraint names remain `getDisplayMedia`-only; retire if `getUserMedia`
  ever honours them.
- **(check:stt-error-map-has-default)** The Web Speech error-name set is open: it is a spec
  enum today, but Chrome has shipped names outside the original list and a vendor-prefixed
  engine can invent one at any release. A mapping switch with no `default:` arm returns
  `undefined` for such a name, every downstream comparison on the kind is then false, and the
  dialog policy silently takes its do-nothing arm. Reaffirm while the error vocabulary can
  grow; retire if the set is closed and versioned.
- **(check:stt-interim-results-gated)** Interim hypotheses arrive on the same `result` event
  as the finished utterance, so enabling `interimResults` does not open a second channel —
  only `isFinal` distinguishes a guess from a transcript. A handler that delivers without
  gating hands the caller a half-heard fragment, then the next, several times per utterance:
  the `"heart heart"` shape. Reaffirm while interim and final share one event; retire if the
  API separates them.
- **(check:stt-terminal-handlers)** A recognition cycle has three exits and only one is
  `result`: `end` fires when the recognizer closes with nothing (a silent user, an endpoint
  the engine gave up on, an OS-level device grab) and `error` on the named failures, of which
  `aborted` arrives on every `stop()` and every barge-in. A recognizer wired for `result`
  alone leaves its cycle pending on two of its three exits, with the UI still showing a live
  mic. Reaffirm while all three events can terminate a cycle; retire if the API guarantees a
  single terminal event.
- **(check:tts-speak-settles)** Both engines end an utterance in more ways than "it
  finished": `chrome.tts` reports `interrupted` whenever a later `speak()` with
  `enqueue: false` displaces it and `cancelled` when it is dropped before starting, and
  `speechSynthesis` reports a failed utterance through `error` and never through `end`. In
  any app that can speak twice or stop early those are the common path, not edge cases, so a
  handler resolving on `end` alone leaves the awaiting caller pending forever with nothing
  thrown and nothing logged. Reaffirm while the terminal-event sets stand; retire if either
  engine collapses them into one.

input.title: Consolidate the fleet's local packs: one per repo, promote what the canon should own
input.body:
Four of the fleet's sixteen members carry more than one local pack. This is the plan to bring each to one pack named for its repo, and to move onto the canon shelf the three facets that were never repo-specific to begin with.

## What the survey found

| Repo | Local packs today | After |
|---|---|---|
| CrosswordChat | `browser-speech`, `host-page-adaptation` | `crossword-chat` |
| EdFringeNow | `edfringe`, `edfringe-data`, `edfringe-requirements` | `edfringe-now` |
| LaughCounter | `laughcounter`, `macos-audio`, `on-device-privacy` | `laugh-counter` |
| MissingBulbWebsite | `repo-mechanics`, `session-tooling`, `site-copy` | `missingbulb-website` |

The other twelve members have exactly one local pack each; none has zero.

Two findings shaped the plan. **The canon already owned two of the three domains.** `packs/web-speech` and `packs/macos` cover most of what `browser-speech` and `macos-audio` say — the same traps, the same measured numbers — and neither CrosswordChat nor LaughCounter had ever declared them. They built local packs beside canon packs they did not know they could adopt, so the same rules were being maintained twice. **The third was genuinely uncovered:** nothing in the corpus addressed operating a web app you do not own, which is why `host-page` is a new pack rather than a merge.

`MissingBulbWebsite/repo-mechanics` has an empty `RULES.md` — one heading line, no rules, no checks — and is deleted rather than merged.

## Phases

- [ ] **Canon promotion** — `packs/web-speech` widened, `packs/macos` widened, `packs/host-page` created. Exit: all three on `main` with the pack catalog regenerated.
- [ ] **EdFringeNow** — three local packs merged to `edfringe-now`. No canon dependency. Exit: one directory under `.claudinite/local/packs/` on that repo's `main`.
- [ ] **MissingBulbWebsite** — `session-tooling` + `site-copy` merged to `missingbulb-website`, `repo-mechanics` deleted. No canon dependency. Exit: as above.
- [ ] **CrosswordChat** — declare canon `web-speech` + `host-page`, delete `browser-speech`, reduce `host-page-adaptation` to its repo-specific residue as `crossword-chat`. Blocked by the canon promotion.
- [ ] **LaughCounter** — declare canon `macos`, delete `macos-audio`, merge `laughcounter` + `on-device-privacy` to `laugh-counter`. Blocked by the canon promotion.

The two member phases that declare canon packs cannot be written before the canon promotion merges: what they carry is vendored output of that PR, so their diff does not exist until review has fixed its shape. They are filed as chain links rather than written into the approved stack, and each link's brief opens by reading its dependency's artifact on `main` — the pack directory in the member's mount — rather than trusting that this issue closed.

## Predicted diffs and policies

| Link | Touches | Size | Policy |
|---|---|---|---|
| Canon promotion | `packs/web-speech/`, `packs/macos/`, `packs/host-page/`, `packs/directory.GENERATED.md` | ~1,900 lines, mostly ported checks and their tests | `nothing` — a new pack's first render is a shelf entry, and nothing checkable stands in for a person's eyes on it |
| EdFringeNow | `.claudinite/local/packs/`, `.claudinite-settings.json` | prose move, ~940 lines relocated | `under:.claudinite/` |
| MissingBulbWebsite | `.claudinite/local/packs/`, `.claudinite-settings.json` | prose move, ~150 lines | `under:.claudinite/` |
| CrosswordChat | `.claudinite/`, `vitest.config.js` | pack deletion + vendored mount | `nothing` — deletes a declared pack |
| LaughCounter | `.claudinite/` | pack deletion + vendored mount | `nothing` — deletes a declared pack |

Three `nothing` links: that is the plan's honest prediction of the review workload.

## Noted, not fixed here

- `edfringe-now` lands at ~940 lines in one `RULES.md`, roughly three times the next-largest local pack in the fleet. Merging all three was the owner's explicit call; the size is worth a follow-up split along the surfaces the merged headings already name, not a reason to hold the merge.
- `MissingBulbWebsite/session-tooling`'s 134 lines are not about that repo — they are session and MCP tooling traps, duplicated in at least three members including Shepherd. Folding them into a repo-named pack entrenches the duplication. The canon is where they belong, on the same argument this plan applies to `web-speech` and `macos`.
- `packs/claudinite-growth/VERSIONS.md` claims version `60903.5` on two rows (lines 10 and 44), which fails `pack-version-claimed-once` on `main` today. Pre-existing and unrelated to this work; filed separately.

The canon-side half of #1691.

`packs/web-speech` and `packs/macos` already own most of what CrosswordChat's `local/browser-speech` and LaughCounter's `local/macos-audio` say. Neither member had declared the canon pack, so each maintained a second copy of rules the shelf already carried. This lands the residue where the territory is already owned, and opens one new pack for the facet nothing covered.

**`web-speech`** takes the six API-contract checks — `mic-capture-released`, `mic-constraints-not-screen-capture`, `stt-error-map-has-default`, `stt-interim-results-gated`, `stt-terminal-handlers`, `tts-speak-settles` — and two rules: interim results as a "still speaking" signal rather than input, and the application-level guard for your own spoken output. That second one is the material find. Chrome's automatic echo cancellation is a loopback of *page* playout, so it attenuates `speechSynthesis` and never sees `chrome.tts`, whose audio the OS renders — which is why the guard belongs in the application and why reaching for a capture constraint means it never gets written. Two existing rules each gain one clause the local pack carried and this one did not.

**`macos`** takes `swift-toolchain-gate` only. Its prose already stated the rule; the check was the missing half. The local pack's other two checks are hardcoded to `mac/Sources/` and `AudioHub.swift`, and canon already holds generalized equivalents in `signal-teardown-routing` and `sudden-termination-vs-teardown`, so they do not come across.

**`host-page`** is new: being a guest in a web app you do not own — reading its DOM, driving it with synthetic input, watching it change, injecting UI into it. `web-scraping` acquires a site's data from outside it, `chrome-extension` covers reaching the page, `headless-browser` drives a browser you own; none covers what to do once you are inside somebody else's. Eleven rules and three checks, generalized off CrosswordChat's `local/host-page-adaptation`. Declared by hand — a content script, a `dispatchEvent` and a `MutationObserver` are equally the shapes of code running on its own page, so no honest fingerprint separates a guest from a host.

All nine checks keep their red-first tests, ported from vitest to `node --test`.

input.head: claude/multiple-local-packs-o1ngro
input.body:
Closes #1692

CrosswordChat and LaughCounter each grew a local pack beside a canon pack they had never declared, so the same rules were being maintained twice. This lands the residue where the canon already owns the territory, and opens one new pack for the facet nothing covered.

## `packs/web-speech` — widened

Six API-contract checks and two rules, from CrosswordChat's `local/browser-speech`.

The rules canon already carried are untouched: the screen-capture constraint trap, the 1.2 s / 1.8 s endpoint window, the biasing gate, the error taxonomy, the lazy voice list, the `chrome.tts` relay. What is new:

- **Interim results are a signal, not input.** They arrive on the *same* `result` event as the finished utterance and are revised several times per utterance, so a handler that delivers `results[i][0].transcript` acts on words the user had not finished saying — and acts again on each revision.
- **The echo guard belongs in the application, not at the capture layer.** Chrome's automatic echo cancellation is a loopback of *page* playout: it attenuates `speechSynthesis` and never sees `chrome.tts`, whose audio the OS renders. That residual echo cannot be reached by any capture constraint, which is why matching the transcript against what you just spoke is the design rather than a stopgap — and why reaching for `suppressLocalAudioPlayback` means the guard that would have worked never gets written.

Two existing rules each take one clause: run the mic preflight even when permission is already granted (otherwise the device is warmed only on the first grant), and treat voice order and speaking rate as user-facing settings rather than constants.

The six checks are pack-level rather than skill-bundled, since they judge the API contracts themselves rather than where the code runs. All six parse the call site rather than grepping for a name, comments stripped first — so a wrapper that delegates its terminal handling, a constraints object hoisted into a constant, and a switch that dispatches side effects rather than mapping a value all stay quiet. What unites them is that their breach is **silent**: nothing throws, nothing logs, and the app keeps showing a live session while the user is heard by nobody.

## `packs/macos` — widened

`swift-toolchain-gate` only. The pack's prose already carried the rule — `/usr/bin/swift` is a stub present on every Mac that pops an 8 GB install prompt rather than failing, so `command -v swift` must sit behind `xcode-select -p`. The check was the missing half.

LaughCounter's other two local checks do not come across: they are hardcoded to `mac/Sources/` and `AudioHub.swift`, and canon already holds generalized equivalents in `signal-teardown-routing` and `sudden-termination-vs-teardown`. `references.md` is created here on its first entry.

## `packs/host-page` — new

Being a guest in a web app you do not own. `web-scraping` acquires a site's data from outside it, `chrome-extension` covers how your code reaches the page, `headless-browser` drives a browser you own — none covers what to do once you are inside somebody else's page.

Eleven rules, generalized off CrosswordChat's `local/host-page-adaptation` with its evidence citations stripped (the `xwd__` token, `page-adapter/`, the REQ ids, the fixture paths). Three checks, sharing one failure mode: an observer that outlives its feature, a synthetic event that does not bubble, and one aimed outside the app root all leave `dispatchEvent` returning true and the page simply not responding — indistinguishable from "the app rejects untrusted events", which is the wrong conclusion and an expensive one to back out of.

Declared by hand. There is no honest fingerprint: a content script, a `dispatchEvent` and a `MutationObserver` are equally the shapes of code running on its *own* page, so a marker that cannot tell a guest from a host would suspect the pack in every DOM repo in the fleet.

## Folders touched

```
packs/web-speech/     6 checks + shared call-site helpers, 2 rules and 2 clauses,
                      references entries for all six, rule index and checks table
packs/macos/          swift-toolchain-gate + its test, references.md created
packs/host-page/      new pack: manifest, 11 rules, 3 checks, README index,
                      references, badge, VERSIONS
packs/                directory.GENERATED.md regenerated for the new pack
```

## Verification

Full canon suite, `node --test` over the CI test roots: **3,214 of 3,217 pass**. All nine new checks are covered both ways — firing on a violating source and silent on the legitimate spellings that a text scan would false-alarm on.

Three failures, none from this diff:

- `packs/claudinite-growth/VERSIONS.md` claims `60903.5` on two rows (lines 10 and 44), failing `pack-version-claimed-once`. Pre-existing on `main` — `git show origin/main:packs/claudinite-growth/VERSIONS.md` shows both rows. Filed as #1693.
- `engine-pack-lane-shims` reports "this checkout is too shallow to walk origin/main's pack history". An artifact of this container's `--depth 1` clone; CI checks out with `fetch-depth: 0`.
- `dev/tools/tests/badges.test.mjs` flagged the new badge as untracked before it was staged; green once committed.

I have not run the canon's own conformance sweep beyond the test suite, so CI is the first full signal on that half.

`packs/claudinite-growth/VERSIONS.md` claims version `60903.5` on two separate rows — line 10 (the `logs-prune` retention default, #1620) and line 44 (`writing-pack-prose` / `writing-tasks` force-loading, #1648). `packs/claudinite-canon-curation/test/pack-version-claimed-once.test.mjs` fails on this:

```
packs/claudinite-growth/VERSIONS.md: version 60903.5 is claimed by two rows (also line 10),

```

Pre-existing on `main` — confirmed with `git show origin/main:packs/claudinite-growth/VERSIONS.md`, which carries both rows. Surfaced while running the full suite for #1693; unrelated to that change, which touches neither the pack nor the file.

The fix is a judgment call this issue does not pre-empt: one of the two rows takes a later number, and which one depends on what was actually released under `60903.5` — the released artifact decides it, not the file.

input.body:
This repo carries three local packs — `repo-mechanics`, `session-tooling` and `site-copy` — where one will do. It is one of four members in the fleet with more than one; the fleet-wide plan is missingbulb/Claudinite#1691.

None of the three earns separate standing. None carries a single check, so the split buys no enforcement boundary; and `repo-mechanics` has an **empty** `RULES.md` — one heading line, `worldRules: []`, `workRules: []` — so it contributes nothing to a session at all while still costing a directory, a manifest and a row in the rules index.

Merge `session-tooling` and `site-copy` into `missingbulb-website`, grouped under a heading per surface, and drop `repo-mechanics` rather than merging an empty file.

Worth recording rather than fixing here: `session-tooling`'s 134 lines are not about this repo. They are session and MCP tooling traps — the `fields` size knob, `codeload` blocked through the proxy, `enable_pr_auto_merge` never arming, `converge-item.mjs` — and the same lessons are duplicated in at least three fleet members. Folding them into a repo-named pack keeps them working but entrenches the duplication; the canon is where they belong, on the same argument that moved `browser-speech` and `macos-audio` there. Tracked in missingbulb/Claudinite#1691.

input.head: claude/multiple-local-packs-o1ngro
input.body:
Closes #319

Part of the fleet-wide consolidation in missingbulb/Claudinite#1691 — one local pack per repo, named for the repo.

Three packs become one. None of them carried a single check, so the split bought no enforcement boundary; what it bought was three manifests, three directories and three rows in the rules index for eight rules.

**`repo-mechanics` is dropped, not merged.** Its `RULES.md` was one heading line with nothing under it and both rule arrays empty — it contributed nothing to a session while still costing a mount entry. Deleting it is the whole of its migration.

**`session-tooling` and `site-copy` merge** under a heading each, rules demoted one level and otherwise byte-for-byte unchanged. One heading is reworded — "is enough for a small, fixed tool roster" → "settles a small, fixed roster" — because the extra `#` pushed it one byte over the 100-byte line limit `rules-line-length` enforces.

input.head: claude/multiple-local-packs-o1ngro
input.body:
Closes #612

Part of the fleet-wide consolidation in missingbulb/Claudinite#1691 — one local pack per repo, named for the repo.

`edfringe`, `edfringe-data` and `edfringe-requirements` become `edfringe-now`, under a heading per surface: working in the repo, the data pipeline, the requirements harness. All seven checks and both tasks move under the one manifest unchanged.

The split bought no routing anyone used. All three were declared by hand, none was fingerprinted, and a session loaded all three together on every turn — so the only thing three manifests separated was which file a rule was typed into.

## What moved, and what followed it

Two file collisions resolved: `edfringe-data/README.md` becomes `DATA.md` beside the rules it explains, and its `pack.test.mjs` becomes `data-checks.test.mjs`.

Three references followed the rename rather than being left dangling — a grep sweep after the move, not before:

- **`package.json` and `scripts/verify.sh`** both spell `.claudinite/local/packs/edfringe/tasks/` explicitly in their `node --test` globs. Left alone, both tasks' tests would have silently stopped running while everything still went green. (The pack's own `test-globs-in-step` check exists to catch these two drifting apart — it does not catch them drifting *together*.)
- **The caching rule** cross-referenced `edfringe-data/RULES.md`, which is now a section of the same file.

One path is deliberately **not** updated: the `claudinite-isolation` rule quotes a comment a past sweep wrote (`"see the declarations under .claudinite/local/packs/edfringe/tasks/"`). That is a record of a specific past edit, so it stays verbatim.

The local `VERSIONS.md` files do not come across — a local pack is neither versioned nor distributed, and its commits are the record.

## Folders touched

```
.claudinite/local/packs/   three packs become edfringe-now; 7 checks, 2 tasks, tests moved
.claudinite/               claudinite-rules.GENERATED.md regenerated
.claudinite-settings.json  three declarations become one
scripts/, package.json     the node --test globs follow the tasks directory rename
```

## Verification

- `npm test` — **274 pass, 0 fail**.
- `node .claudinite/shared/engine/checks/check_the_world.mjs` — **exit 0, 0 blocking**.

The checks earned their keep on the way: three `config` findings for the stale declarations, one `rules-index-current` for the unimported new pack, and a `rules-line-length` advisory. One assertion inside `pack.test.mjs` needed its expected string repointed after the rename — the check was right, the expectation was stale.

Three `file-placement` advisories remain in `plan/lib/`. They are pre-existing on `main` and this diff touches none of that code.

## Noted, not fixed here

The merged `RULES.md` is ~940 lines and 34 rules, roughly three times the next-largest local pack in the fleet. Merging all three was the explicit call and I have not second-guessed it, but a file that long is scanned by heading rather than read — and the three headings this PR introduces are the seams a later split would follow. Recorded on #612 rather than treated as free.

input.body:
Blocked-by: missingbulb/Claudinite#1693

Part of the fleet-wide consolidation in missingbulb/Claudinite#1691 — one local pack per repo, named for the repo.

This repo carries two local packs, `browser-speech` and `host-page-adaptation`, and declares neither of the canon packs that now own their territory. `browser-speech` was written beside `packs/web-speech`, which already covered most of what it says — the same traps, the same measured numbers — and `host-page-adaptation` has now been promoted to a new canon pack, `packs/host-page`.

## What makes this step's world ready

`packs/host-page/` and the widened `packs/web-speech/` are on Claudinite's `main`, and this repo's vendored mount carries them. **Read that before doing anything else**: check `.claudinite/shared/packs/host-page/pack.mjs` exists in this repo after a re-vendor, and that `packs/directory.GENERATED.md` in the mount lists `host-page`. If it does not, missingbulb/Claudinite#1693 has not landed (or landed and was reverted) — comment what you read and leave this issue **open**. Do not build on the assumption that it merged; the blocking issue closing is not the same as the artifact being there.

## The work

1. Declare canon `web-speech` and `host-page` in `.claudinite-settings.json`, at the versions canon publishes, and re-vendor (the `adopt-pack` skill owns this).
2. Delete `local/browser-speech` entirely. Every rule and all six checks are in canon `web-speech` now; nothing repo-specific was left in it.
3. Reduce `local/host-page-adaptation` to `local/crossword-chat`: the general rules and all three checks went to canon, so what remains is this repo's own instances — the `xwd__` arch-test token and the `page-adapter/` quarantine it enforces, the NYT ~30 s idle timer and the bare-`Shift` nudge, the pencil button's unreadable ON state, the fixture and `localhost:8787` setup, the `selectors.js` provenance record, and the REQ ids. Expect a much smaller file than the 158 lines it starts from; if a rule reads as general when you get to it, it belongs in canon, not here.
4. Update `vitest.config.js` — it includes `.claudinite/local/packs`, and the pack test files move with the rename.
5. Update both packs' README references and the routing guidance, which currently point `excludes` at `local/browser-speech`.

## What counts as this having worked

`node .claudinite/shared/engine/checks/check_the_world.mjs` exits 0, `npm test` passes, and `.claudinite/local/packs/` holds exactly one directory, `crossword-chat`. A session started afterwards loads the canon speech and host-page rules and this repo's residue, with nothing duplicated between them.

## How it ends

input.title: Declare canon macos; merge the three local packs into laugh-counter
input.body:
Blocked-by: missingbulb/Claudinite#1693

Part of the fleet-wide consolidation in missingbulb/Claudinite#1691 — one local pack per repo, named for the repo.

This repo carries three local packs and does not declare canon `macos`, which already owns almost everything `local/macos-audio` says: never construct an engine to ask whether a device exists (down to the `CADefaultDeviceAggregate-<pid>-<n>` detail), presence is not usability at either layer, a duration is a claim about a span you observed, `Date()` versus `systemUptime`, generation-guarded deferred work, coalescing by id, "started" is not "working", compile-green is not a gate, and the `xcode-select -p` toolchain gate. The local pack has been maintaining a second copy of the canon's own rules.

## What makes this step's world ready

Canon `packs/macos` carries `swift-toolchain-gate` and this repo's vendored mount has it. **Read that first**: `.claudinite/shared/packs/macos/worldRules/swift-toolchain-gate.mjs` exists after a re-vendor. If it does not, missingbulb/Claudinite#1693 has not landed — comment what you read and leave this issue **open** rather than proceeding on the assumption that it did.

## The work

1. Declare canon `macos` in `.claudinite-settings.json` at the version canon publishes, and re-vendor (the `adopt-pack` skill owns this).
2. Delete `local/macos-audio`. Its `signal-teardown-routing` and its `no-sudden-termination` declared check have generalized equivalents in canon (`signal-teardown-routing`, `sudden-termination-vs-teardown`), and `swift-toolchain-gate` is now canon's. Before deleting, diff its prose against canon `packs/macos/RULES.md` and keep only what canon genuinely lacks — carry that into `laugh-counter` rather than losing it.
3. `input-node-confined` is the one check that cannot generalize: it names `AudioHub` and `mac/Sources/`. Keep it as a local check under `laugh-counter`.
4. Merge `laughcounter` and `on-device-privacy` into `laugh-counter`, under a heading each, keeping both of `on-device-privacy`'s checks (`on-device-speech`, `single-storage-directory`).
5. Drop the local `VERSIONS.md` files — a local pack is neither versioned nor distributed.

Note on the privacy pack while merging it: its own text says the boundary "is the product requirement (`docs/DESIGN-AND-TRADEOFFS.md` §0/§6, README *Privacy*)", so its prose half largely restates a requirement rather than constraining how work is done. Its mechanical half is correctly checks. It is merged as-is here; whether that prose should instead live as an executable requirement is a separate question this repo cannot answer until it adopts `executable-requirements`, which it does not currently declare. Do not resolve that in this change.

## What counts as this having worked

`node .claudinite/shared/engine/checks/check_the_world.mjs` exits 0, `swift build` still succeeds, and `.claudinite/local/packs/` holds exactly one directory, `laugh-counter`. A session started afterwards loads canon's macOS rules plus this repo's own, with nothing duplicated between them.

Watch for one thing specific to this repo: nothing here runs on `pull_request` outside `mac/**`, so a PR touching only `.claudinite/` starts no checks at all and is mergeable the moment it opens. "CI will catch it" is false here — the local check run above is the whole verification.

## How it ends

CI is red on one test, and it is not this PR's.

`test-and-conformance` reports **3,216 of 3,217 passing**. The single failure is `the canon's own packs claim every version exactly once`:

```
packs/claudinite-growth/VERSIONS.md: version 60903.5 is claimed by two rows
(also line 10), so two changes shipped under one number
```

This diff touches neither `packs/claudinite-growth/` nor any version file outside `packs/web-speech`, `packs/macos` and the new `packs/host-page`. The duplicate is already on `main` — `git show origin/main:packs/claudinite-growth/VERSIONS.md` carries both rows, line 10 (`logs-prune` retention default, #1620) and line 44 (`writing-pack-prose` force-loading, #1648). Filed separately as #1694.

There is no fix to port — no open PR addresses it — so I am not widening this PR to carry one. The reason is not tidiness: the fix requires deciding **which** of the two rows takes a new number, and that depends on what was actually released under `60903.5`. Members may already hold that version, so renumbering the wrong row rewrites history they have. The released artifact settles it, not the file, and that is a call for #1694 rather than a drive-by here.

So this PR cannot go green until #1694 lands. Everything in this diff is verified: all nine new checks pass both ways, the pack catalog regenerates clean, and the two local failures I saw that CI did not (`engine-pack-lane-shims` on a shallow clone, and the badge before it was staged) are both absent here.

Three PRs open, all subscribed. Here's where it landed.

**[missingbulb/Claudinite#1693](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/pull/1693)** — the canon promotion. Two packs widened, one created.

```
packs/web-speech/     6 API-contract checks + shared call-site helpers, 2 new rules
                      (interim-results gating, the application-level echo guard),
                      2 clauses folded into existing rules, references entries for
                      all six checks, rule index and checks table
packs/macos/          swift-toolchain-gate + its test; references.md created
packs/host-page/      new pack — manifest, 11 rules, 3 checks, README index,
                      references, badge, VERSIONS
packs/                directory.GENERATED.md regenerated
```

**[missingbulb/EdFringeNow#613](https://github.com/missingbulb/EdFringeNow/pull/613)** — three packs into `edfringe-now`.

```
.claudinite/local/packs/   3 packs → 1; 7 checks, 2 tasks, tests relocated
.claudinite-settings.json  3 declarations → 1
scripts/, package.json     node --test globs follow the tasks directory rename
```

**[missingbulb/MissingBulbWebsite#320](https://github.com/missingbulb/MissingBulbWebsite/pull/320)** — three into `missingbulb-website`.

```
.claudinite/local/packs/   session-tooling + site-copy merged; repo-mechanics deleted
.claudinite-settings.json  3 declarations → 1
```

**On your instructions, two changes.** `host-page` is the canon name for `host-page-adaptation` — it names the territory the way `web-scraping` and `chrome-extension` do. And the promotions turned out to be *merges*: canon already had `web-speech` and `macos`, carrying most of those rules verbatim in substance, which CrosswordChat and LaughCounter had simply never declared.

**Verification.** EdFringeNow `npm test` 274/274 and world checks exit 0; MissingBulbWebsite checks exit 0; canon suite 3,216/3,217 in CI. The checks earned their keep — four blocking findings on MissingBulbWebsite and four on EdFringeNow, including `package.json` and `verify.sh` globs that name the tasks directory explicitly and would have silently stopped running both tasks' tests while everything stayed green.

**What's blocked.** Canon CI is red on one test that isn't mine: `packs/claudinite-growth/VERSIONS.md` claims `60903.5` on two rows, pre-existing on `main`, filed as [#1694](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/issues/1694). CrosswordChat and LaughCounter are filed as chain links ([CrosswordChat#396](https://github.com/missingbulb/CrosswordChat/issues/396), [LaughCounter#394](https://github.com/missingbulb/LaughCounter/issues/394)), each `Blocked-by:` #1693, because what they'd carry is vendored output of it. Each brief opens by reading the artifact on `main` rather than trusting that the blocker closed. Plan and predicted diffs are on [#1691](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/issues/1691).

Two things I recorded rather than fixed: `edfringe-now`'s `RULES.md` is ~940 lines across 34 rules, and `session-tooling`'s 134 lines aren't about MissingBulbWebsite at all — they're fleet-general session tooling traps duplicated in at least three members, which the canon should own on the same argument that moved the other two.

> ⚠️ Still open: **#1694** needs your decision on which `claudinite-growth` row takes a new version — [#1693](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/pull/1693) stays red until then, and the two chain links stay blocked behind it. [#320](https://github.com/missingbulb/MissingBulbWebsite/pull/320) is green; [#613](https://github.com/missingbulb/EdFringeNow/pull/613) had `ci` green with `ui-requirements` still running. All three are subscribed, so I'll act on events as they arrive.

   Regenerate lockfiles and generated files with the repo's tooling, never
   by hand; then validate and push. Never rewrite history on someone else's
   branch: no rebase, amend, or force-push (a merge commit keeps their
   checkout valid); on a branch you created, follow the repo's convention.
   Ask only when both sides changed the same logic and picking either loses
   behavior.
2. **CI red** → first rule out a failure that isn't this PR's: an error naming
   a service the diff doesn't touch that reproduces identically on one
   re-run, or a check red on the base branch too. When a fix for it exists
   (any PR whose change you have read and expect to get this PR green,
   the breaking commit's own revert, or a fix PR you opened yourself),
   port the same change into this PR now and push: it no-ops once the
   base carries it, and waiting on that PR to merge, your own included,
   is still waiting. Standing down on such a failure, ported or not, is
   never silent: one comment on the PR (to the user instead on a PR you
   only watch) naming the failing check, why it is not this PR's, and the
   fix you ported or that none exists yet, then the one re-run below, if
   unspent. Anything else is this PR's to root-cause: fix and push when
   it is in code the PR touches or breaks; when it is in code unrelated to
   the change, port a fix that exists (as above, your own fix PR included)
   and push, and only when none exists say what is failing and why, with
   a proposed patch, rather than widening the PR (a ported fix is not
   widening).
   "Flake" is not a root cause: re-run a job only to confirm that first
   case, as the one re-run after that standing-down comment, or if it died
   before any test body ran (checkout, install, runner loss) or passed
   earlier on this exact commit; at most once in total, if you have the
   means, and a second failure is real. If you judge a
   failure a flake but lack the means to re-run (no permission, a 403):
   if the flaky test can be made robust within this PR's scope, push that
   fix; otherwise say so once, then keep the PR watched (a check-in
   scheduled until it is done, merged or closed), never idle on a red PR
   you own. Never skip, disable, or
   quarantine a test to get green; never push an empty commit or close and
   reopen the PR to kick CI.
3. **Review comments** → implement and push small, local asks from reviewers (nits,
   renames, lint-bot fixes, an added test, a one-function refactor). Can't
   tell whether a human reviewer's ask is small → treat it as large. Larger
   asks from a human reviewer (multi-file refactors, API or schema changes,
   open-ended design feedback) on a PR you did not open → reply with your
   proposal, never push or resolve: the author decides (when the author is
   your user, put the proposal to them here). "Design-level" never excuses a
   review bot's finding, a CI failure, or your own reading of the diff: bot
   findings are bug reports, so verify them and push the fix. There is no
   round limit: repeated findings on your pushes mean fix the root cause,
   not stop. On a PR you opened or were asked to drive for its author, also
   resolve the threads you addressed, answer intent questions from the
   diff, and re-request the human reviewer after pushing for their
   changes-requested review.

# Owner interaction preferences

Personal preferences from the repo owner for how the assistant should interact — tone, summary style, end-of-turn conventions, how results and decisions are surfaced, and the phrases the owner uses to trigger defined commands. These are **not** project conventions (those live in the [packs/](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/tree/main/packs) corpus, each pack bundling its skills); they're how the owner likes to be worked with. Where a preference triggers a command whose mechanics are a project convention, the mechanics stay in their own doc and the entry here just owns the trigger phrase.

## Preferences

- **End every turn with a blockquote callout** — `> ✅ All done`, or `> ⚠️ Still open: …` listing what remains — never hedged in prose.
- **"LGTM"** merges the change at hand into `main` (`merge-to-main` skill); it approves that change only, never later work.
- **"bump version"** raises the project's version; the project's own workflow decides how it changes and which files change.
- **In the conversation**: link every source-controlled document you edit, display every image you edit, link every issue/PR number.
- **Ask every decision or approval through an `AskUserQuestion` popup, never prose** — one question per item, each with its case.
- **Enclose anything the owner will lift elsewhere** — a prompt, a message, copy to paste — in one delimited block, boundaries unmistakable.
- **Prefix a prompt for another session, inside its block, with a disclaimer**: Claude wrote it — examine inconsistencies, don't follow blindly.
- **Open a pull request right after committing to a branch**, unasked — overriding Claude Code's default of waiting to be told.
- **When handing over a PR to review, describe the folders the change touched in the conversation, in a text box** — a brief line per folder saying what changed there. Show non-test folders only, and ignore README files, comment-only changes, and history-keeping updates (a version bump, a changelog or `VERSIONS.md` row).
- **Keep working through a multi-step plan without pausing for approval of each step** — aggregate the steps into one substantial change to review, and stop only for an action that reaches the world (a release, a fleet-wide effect, anything irreversible) or a decision only the owner can make.
- **Never schedule a self check-in to poll a PR** — no recurring wake-up, routine, or `send_later` re-arm that re-reads a PR's state, CI or mergeability on a timer. Act on PR events when they arrive; when nothing has arrived, end the turn.

- session-start-hook: Creating and developing startup hooks for Claude Code on the web. Use when the user wants to set up a repository for Claude Code on the web, create a SessionStart hook to ensure their project can run tests and linters during web sessions.

- adopt-pack: Add one or more packs to an already-adopted Claudinite member — declare, run each pack's adoption interview, re-vendor, scaffold, land. Use when asked to adopt, add, enable, or declare a pack (e.g. product-wiki, executable-requirements) on a repo that already runs Claudinite.
- authoring-agent-docs: How to write instruction files coding agents follow reliably. Use before writing or editing any Claude instruction doc — a project CLAUDE.md, a convention doc, a routine spec.
- bug-investigation: Method for investigating a bug and pinning down its root cause. Use when investigating a bug report, when a fix didn't hold or a bug recurs, or when a report doesn't reproduce against main.
- ci-performance-evaluation: Method for finding where a repo's CI time actually goes and what is worth fixing. Use when CI feels slow, when investigating a runtime regression, or when the weekly ci-performance task hands you a finding.
- do-later: File a change to be made AFTER the work in flight — a well-defined issue, marked for the queue and blocked behind the current PR/issue and behind the previous deferral, so repeated asks chain. Use when the owner says "/do-later …", "do this after this lands", or otherwise defers a change instead of derailing the session.
- extract-from-activity: Mine a window of a repo's commits, merged PRs and issue activity for durable, reusable lessons and land them in the repo's own local packs. Use when extracting lessons from repo artifacts — the growth-extract task's activity half, or an owner asking what a recent stretch of work taught.
- extract-from-conversations: Mine an agent-user conversation — a captured conversation log or the live session — for friction-driven lessons (misunderstandings, backtracks, measured wall-time waits) and land them in the repo's own local packs. Use when extracting lessons from a session transcript or the conversation-logs branch, or when an owner asks for a retrospective.
- file-placement: Where a file should live — the reference-distance metric, the high-reach code smell, and the mandated-location, test-location and plugin-contract exemptions. Use before placing, moving, or renaming a file, or when reviewing where one lives.
- fleet-triage: Survey every open issue across the whole missingbulb fleet, split the queue items from the plain ones, and attribute each parked task to the cause that actually parked it. Use when asked for a triage run, a fleet overview, a stuck-tasks analysis, or "all open issues across the fleet".
- git-github-advanced: Git/GitHub procedures beyond the baseline lifecycle. Use for commit layering, recovering a branch after a squash-merge, CI-trigger rules, GitHub Actions gotchas, or merge-relocation traps.
- github-actions-scheduling: What a GitHub Actions `schedule:` trigger actually guarantees — late fires, dropped fires, the 60-day disable — and how to build and describe scheduled work around it. Use when adding, changing, explaining, or debugging anything that runs on a cron in GitHub Actions.
- growth-dedup: Prune a repo's local packs of items the mounted Claudinite canon now covers — remove, strip to residue, or track a wording drift, never grow an entry. Use when the growth dedup task runs, or when asked to reconcile or dedup local packs against the canon.
- improve-comments: Improve the comments in a repo's own source — delete the ones that restate the code or narrate a past edit, correct the ones that have drifted from what the code now does, and add the why where only a reader's guess carries it. Use when working a repo's comments as their own pass (the tidy-repo pack's improve-comments task), never as a side effect of another change.
- merge-to-main: Merge the change in front of the owner into main. Use when the owner says "LGTM" or asks to merge/land the current branch or PR into main.
- production-retrospective: Design and file the review that comes back on its own once a larger element has lived in production long enough to judge — is it working, misused, overused, underused — read from its real production record against expectations written down when the element was designed. Use when designing a larger element (the brief is authored then), when filing a migration plan's chain (the retrospective is its last link), when a merge completes a design-doc'd element, or when defining a new retrospective class for a pack, a repo, or the fleet.
- prose-to-checks: Mine pack prose (RULES.md, SKILL.md) for always-testable rules that were never converted to checks, and convert the strongest ones. Use when auditing packs for convertible rules, when the weekly prose-to-checks sweep runs, or as the upgrade pass over prose a growth-extract run just wrote.
- repo-text-sweeps: Mechanics for grep/sed sweeps, renames, and path relocations across a repo. Use before a bulk find-replace, a rename, or moving files — and after one, to catch silently broken references.
- single-issue-triage: Triage one open issue and take the first applicable action — close-if-implemented, needs-decision, blocked, quick-win, or leave. 1	# Web Speech APIs
2	
3	> Some of these APIs (`chrome.tts`) are extension-only; where a rule touches
4	> MV3 service-worker / content-script mechanics, only the speech-API facet is
5	> here — the general extension gotcha underneath is not.
6	
7	## Speech-to-text (`webkitSpeechRecognition` / Web Speech API)
8	
9	- **The recognizer owns its own microphone capture — you cannot hand it
10	  `getUserMedia` audio constraints.** `echoCancellation` / `noiseSuppression` /
11	  `autoGainControl` are `getUserMedia` *microphone* constraints, and the recognizer
12	  exposes no hook to set them on its internal stream (Chrome applies its default
13	  echo cancellation there regardless). To *warm* the device with a known processing
14	  state — and to read back whether echo cancellation actually engaged — run a
15	  separate preflight `getUserMedia({ audio: {…} })` capture and stop its tracks.
16	  (`suppressLocalAudioPlayback` /
17	  `restrictOwnAudio` are `getDisplayMedia` *screen-capture* constraints and have no
18	  bearing on a mic — don't reach for them here.)
19	- **Read the whole n-best list, not just alternative `[0]`.** Set
20	  `maxAlternatives` > 1 and iterate `result[0..length]` for `{ transcript,
21	  confidence }`; the ranked alternatives are exactly where homophone / near-miss
22	  recovery lives. (1)
23	- **`onresult`, `onend`, and `onerror` all fire — settle the cycle exactly once.**
24	  Guard a `settled` flag: interim results arrive before the final one, a cycle can
25	  end with no result at all (treat `onend`-without-result as `no-speech`), and an
26	  error and an end can both arrive. (2)
27	- **With `interimResults` off, engines omit `isFinal` — treat a result as final
28	  unless `isFinal === false`.** Don't test `if (result.isFinal)` (it's `undefined`
29	  on those engines and you'll drop every result); test `result.isFinal !== false`.
30	- **The classic recognizer streams audio to a cloud service (Google's) — plan for
31	  it.** A `network` error means "offline / service unreachable", and audio leaves
32	  the machine. On-device recognition is opt-in and capability-gated: probe
33	  `SpeechRecognition.available({ langs, processLocally: true }) === 'available'`
34	  once and cache it, set `recognizer.processLocally = true`, and **never trigger a
35	  language-pack download** (only `'available'` counts, not `'downloadable'`). When
36	  the local path is absent, fall back to ordinary cloud recognition unchanged.
37	- **Contextual biasing (`SpeechRecognitionPhrase` + `recognizer.phrases`) works
38	  only on the on-device path** — gate it behind that same availability probe and
39	  apply it best-effort (any failure falls back to un-biased recognition rather than
40	  breaking the listen cycle). Only bias **closed vocabularies you control**
41	  (a command lexicon, known labels, a spelling alphabet) with **modest** boosts:
42	  over-boosting makes the recognizer hear a biased phrase when the user actually
43	  said a same-sounding free-form utterance.
44	- **Map the raw Web Speech error names to a small taxonomy** — `not-allowed` /
45	  `service-not-allowed` → permission-denied, plus `no-speech`, `network`,
46	  `aborted`, `audio-capture`, else `other`. In particular `aborted` is the
47	  *self-inflicted* stop (you called `recognizer.abort()`), so the caller should
48	  ignore it rather than surface it as a failure.
49	- **A missed endpoint mid-utterance needs a pause watchdog, not just `onend`.**
50	  If interim hypotheses exist but no final arrives, the engine may have lost the
51	  endpoint; a timer that fires after a pause discards the half-heard input and
52	  reopens a fresh cycle (preventing "heart heart" doubles when the user repeats
53	  themselves). Set the threshold **well above a natural mid-command thinking
54	  pause** — a tight window (~1.2 s) cuts real commands; a wider one (~1.8 s) keeps
55	  only the genuine missed-endpoint case.
56	- **Mic permission is per-origin, and the grant belongs to whatever page the
57	  recognizer runs in.** In a content script the prompt reads as the *host site*
58	  asking and the grant persists for that origin. Surface it in a controlled moment:
59	  preflight `navigator.permissions.query({ name: 'microphone' })`, then a one-time
60	  `getUserMedia` to raise the prompt. **Retry the capture bare** (`{ audio: true }`)
61	  if the first constrained call is rejected — a browser balking at the constraint
62	  *shape* must not be misread as a permission denial; only a second failure is a
63	  real "denied".
64	
65	## Text-to-speech (`chrome.tts` / `speechSynthesis`)
66	
67	- **Prefer `chrome.tts` over `speechSynthesis` — it's immune to page
68	  autoplay / user-activation gating.** `speechSynthesis` invoked from a content
69	  script is subject to the host page's autoplay policy and can silently refuse to
70	  speak; `chrome.tts` (extension-only, needs the `"tts"` permission, usable from the
71	  service worker) is not. Make `chrome.tts` primary and `speechSynthesis` the
72	  fallback for non-extension document contexts.
73	- **`chrome.tts` doesn't exist in a content script — relay speak/cancel to the
74	  service worker over a port.** Keep the same `speak()`/`cancel()` contract on both
75	  sides; the in-page port sends `{ speak }` / `{ cancel }` messages and the worker
76	  drives `chrome.tts`. On port disconnect, resolve every pending `speak()` promise
77	  so a dead worker never leaves the caller awaiting an utterance that will never
78	  finish.
79	- **Voice lists load lazily — an empty `getVoices()` means "not ready yet", not
80	  "no voices".** Resolve the preferred voice on the *first* `speak()` and don't
81	  cache an empty result: fall back to the default that turn and try to resolve
82	  again next turn.
83	- **Don't trust the OS/browser default voice — it's often the most robotic one
84	  installed.** Keep an ordered list of preferred voice names, take the first one
85	  actually installed, and fall back to the default only when none match.
86	- **Resolve a `speak()` promise on *any* terminal event, and never reject.** For
87	  `chrome.tts` that's `end` / `interrupted` / `cancelled` / `error`; for
88	  `speechSynthesis` it's `onend` / `onerror`. Resolving (not rejecting) on error
89	  keeps a spoken-prompt sequence from deadlocking on one bad utterance. Use
90	  `enqueue: false` so a new line interrupts the current one for turn-taking rather
91	  than stacking up.
92	- **Neither engine reliably supports SSML — you can't force intonation.** If a
93	  punctuation cue matters (a question's rising tone), speak the cue in words
94	  ("question mark") rather than relying on prosody the engine may not apply.

input.title: ui-requirements goldens flap: the same tree fails different cases run to run
input.body:
The `ui-requirements` lane is non-deterministic. The same tree produces different failures on different runs, so a red lane currently says nothing about whether a change broke anything.

## Evidence

Four runs, three different outcomes, across trees whose only differences are under `.claudinite/` (a local-pack consolidation, #612 / #613 — no UI code, and `test:ui` itself untouched):

| Run | Tree | Result |
|---|---|---|
| CI, `ui-requirements` | #613 head `a083751` | fails `shared-money.8.5` — 3346 of 117840 px (2.84%) |
| local `npm run test:ui` | same commit `a083751` | fails `now-commitment.3.6` (1183 of 28512 px, 4.15%) **and** `now-filters.5.6` (animated golden, 81979 bytes committed vs 74845 rendered) |
| local `npm run test:ui` | same commit `a083751`, immediately after | **101/101 pass** |
| local `npm run test:ui` | `origin/main` `b4a2730` | 101/101 pass |

The second and third rows are the load-bearing pair: identical working tree, no re-render of anything between them, two different answers. Four distinct cases have now flapped (`shared-money.8.5`, `now-commitment.3.6`, `now-filters.5.6`), which points at the harness rather than at any one case's capture.

The animated-golden failure is worth noting separately — `now-filters.5.6` compares APNG **bytes**, not pixels, so it is a different comparator from the other two and it flapped as well. Whatever the shared cause is, it is upstream of both comparison paths.

## Why this matters more than an ordinary flake

The pack's own rule says the harness stays at zero pixel tolerance and that *"when the comparison ever flaps, the fix is more determinism, not a tolerance"* — so the remedy is to find what is still unpinned, not to widen the comparator. The determinism levers are all in `product/requirements/shared/harness/`: fixed clock via `page.clock`, fixed geolocation, seeded `Math.random`, route-fulfilled network, frozen animations, the `FONTCONFIG_FILE` font subset, and the pinned Chromium. Something outside that set is still leaking in.

Worth checking first, given the local runs above were on a machine with the fonts subset in play and still flapped: an async settle that `case-helpers.js` does not wait on (the pages settle their async work into observable state — a capture racing that would explain a small, varying pixel delta), and whether `--test-concurrency=1` is actually holding for the behavior lane as well as the screen lane.

## Not fixing it in #613

#613 is a local-pack consolidation. Its only non-`.claudinite/` changes are the pack declaration in `.claudinite-settings.json` and two `node --test` glob strings in `package.json` / `scripts/verify.sh` — neither reachable from a rendered pixel, and `test:ui` is a separate script it does not touch. Making the harness deterministic is a real fix but a different change, and doing it there would widen that PR well past its request.

Four runs, three outcomes, on trees differing only under `.claudinite/`:

| Run | Tree | Result |

| CI `ui-requirements` | `a083751` (this head) | fails `shared-money.8.5` — 3346/117840 px |

| local `npm run test:ui` | `origin/main` `b4a2730` | 101/101 pass |

Rows two and three are the proof: identical working tree, nothing re-rendered between them, two different answers. Four separate cases have flapped, across *both* comparators — `shared-money.8.5` and `now-commitment.3.6` on pixels, `now-filters.5.6` on APNG bytes — so the cause sits upstream of either.

This PR cannot be the cause. Its only changes outside `.claudinite/` are the pack declaration in `.claudinite-settings.json` and two `node --test` glob strings in `package.json` and `scripts/verify.sh`; `test:ui` is a separate script it does not touch, and nothing in the diff is reachable from a rendered pixel. `main` alone passes.

I am not making the harness deterministic here — that is the right fix per the pack's own rule (*"when the comparison ever flaps, the fix is more determinism, not a tolerance"*), but it is a different change and would widen a pack consolidation well past its request. It has its own issue.

content.text:
Both PRs are merged and their conversations captured. Status on the two still open:

**[EdFringeNow#613](https://github.com/missingbulb/EdFringeNow/pull/613)** — LGTM received, but it hit a merge conflict before I could land it. `#611` (`/plan2`) had touched the same two `node --test` glob lines this branch renamed; I kept both sides (plan2's glob *and* the `edfringe-now` path) and revalidated — **282 tests pass**, checks exit 0.

Then `ui-requirements` went red. It isn't this PR's, and it isn't a one-off:

| Run | Tree | Result |
|---|---|---|
| CI | `a083751` | fails `shared-money.8.5` |
| local | `a083751` | fails `now-commitment.3.6` **and** `now-filters.5.6` |
| local, immediately after | `a083751` | **101/101 pass** |
| local | `origin/main` | 101/101 pass |

Identical tree, two different answers. Four cases have flapped across *both* comparators — pixel and APNG-byte — so the cause is upstream of either. My diff's only non-`.claudinite/` changes are a pack declaration and two glob strings; `test:ui` is untouched. Filed as [#615](https://github.com/missingbulb/EdFringeNow/issues/615) with the reproduction, commented on the PR, and spent the one permitted re-run — now waiting on it.

I deliberately did **not** make the harness deterministic here. That's the right fix (the pack's own rule: *more determinism, not a tolerance*), but it would widen a pack consolidation well past its request.

**[Claudinite#1693](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/pull/1693)** — #1694 turned out to be **already fixed on main**: `dcec190` (#1680) renumbered the duplicate row to `60904.3`. Base directory for this skill: /home/user/Shepherd/.claude/skills/verify-in-production

# Verify in production

A change is finished when someone has watched it work. Most changes you can watch **now**, and
that is the rule — this skill is only for the rest: a change whose proof lives somewhere the
repo cannot see yet. You are filing the proof, not doing the work — and the proof itself runs
unattended: an automatic check, end to end, that the run can make from this repository.
Where it cannot, the answer is almost always to file nothing and say the change is
unverified; asking a person is a rare exception, and no automatic check existing is not
on its own enough to earn one.

## When it fires: after the merge, never before

**The PR must have merged.** This skill runs as a step of the merge, unasked — `merge-to-main`
calls it once the squash has landed — and at no other moment. Not when the code is written, not
when the PR opens, not while review is in flight.

The reason is that a PR can be **rejected**, and a branch that is still open can be rewritten
under you. Both leave a verification whose premise never reached `main`:

- A **rewritten branch** makes the brief describe a change that no longer exists. (1)
- A **rejected PR** is worse, because the queue cannot tell it from a merge. A blocked item
  releases on its blocker being *closed*, and nothing reads `merged` — so the item goes ready,
  reads an `In-production-when:` that can never become true, pushes `Not-before:` forward by
  `Retry-every:` without comment, and repeats indefinitely. No janitor rule reclaims it: the
  stale-ready sweep cannot see an item sleeping on a future `Not-before`, and the
  stuck-dependency sweep exempts an item whose blockers have closed.

So there is no such thing as filing this early and letting the queue sort it out. Wait for the
merge, then read **what actually landed** — the merged diff, not the branch you remember writing.

## First: does this file anything at all?

Most changes **file nothing.** Run the test in this order and stop at the first answer:

1. **Can you watch it work in this session — now, or after a wait you can sit through?**
   Then do that and file nothing — the bar is "could you", not "did you already". If it
   becomes readable inside the session you are in, waiting for it is cheaper than every
   mechanism below. (2)
2. **Did a test that ran prove it?** A unit test, a CI job, an executable-requirements or UI
   test covering exactly the behaviour that changed. File nothing — the suite is the mechanism
   that comes back.
3. **Does the change have an observable effect at all?** A comment, a design doc, a README, a
   rename with no behavioural edge, a refactor a passing suite already pins. File nothing.
4. **Otherwise: where does its effect first become observable?** If the answer is a place and a
   moment — a member repo once it converges, a site once it deploys, a session once it reloads
   its rules — that is what you file.

The bar is *could not be watched now*, not *would be nice to double-check*. A verification
filed for a change already covered by a test is a wasted run re-proving what the suite proved.
And the test above only files point assertions: when the merge completes a **larger element** —
one that earned a design doc or a phased tracking issue — the ~week-later review of how the
whole design fared is [production-retrospective](../production-retrospective/SKILL.md)'s
separate call, made beside this one.

## Second: which runner can read it? If neither, file nothing

There are two runners, and the artifact's address decides which one a verification
gets — never preference:

- **A public URL** — a Pages site, a deployed config, a published module, a live
  `/version.json` — files the **coded form**: declarative probes an agentless queue
  task (`claudinite-tasks/verify-production`) fetches and judges Action-side, where
  egress exists. No session ever runs, so there is no egress wall to hit — this is
  the lane for exactly the class that used to park. (3)
- **A GitHub read** — an issue's state, a file at HEAD, a workflow run's conclusion —
  files the **agentic form**: an unattended session on this repository, whose reach
  is narrower than yours — **GitHub, through its own tools, in the repositories its
  routine's scope names** — and nothing else. Take the read you are about to write
  into `Verify:` and answer, in one sentence, *which tool call the run makes, in
  which repository*. **Another repo is the standard trap**, because the read looks
  ordinary and the wall is invisible from here — a `Verify:` naming a member repo
  parks minutes after being picked, on a scope denial. (4)
  A cross-repo artifact with a
  public URL — a member's stamp on `raw.githubusercontent.com`, its Pages site — is
  not walled at all: it is a URL, and the coded form reads it.
- **Neither** — a login-walled console, a private dashboard, a repository outside
  scope with no public surface — **file nothing**: say in your reply that the change
  is unverified and what would prove it. That is a filter, not a fork: an unreadable
  artifact is a reason not to file. Filing anyway spends a session rediscovering the
  wall and then parks `needs-human-action`, which is the human's-memory outcome this
  skill exists to avoid. (3)

Where the subject is the **fleet** rather than this repo — every member's stamp, every
member's CI — this queue is the wrong runner for it whatever you file. It belongs to a
routine that holds fleet scope, if the project has one, and to nobody otherwise.

**Asking a person is the rare exception**, not the fallback. The bar is not "no
automatic check exists" — most changes clear that and still get nothing. It is that a
silent failure here would be **costly**, and you would be willing to interrupt the
person today to have them look. If you would not, the change goes unverified and you say
so. When it does clear that bar, file an ordinary issue — never a queue item: title it
the same `Verify in production: …`, carry `Original-issue:` and attach it as that
issue's sub-issue, and write the body per
[writing-handover-issues](../writing-handover-issues/SKILL.md) — somebody else runs it,
so the checklist is the artifact. **No mark, no
`Not-before:`, no `Retry-every:`, no `Model:`**: nothing in it is the queue's, and a mark
would buy only a session that parks. Assign it to whoever owns the release, and say in
your reply that you are spending their attention and why it was worth it.

## What you file

**A deferred request** — the same ad-hoc lane `/do-later` rides, so the queue does the waiting,
the running and the lifecycle; nothing here adds machinery beside it. One issue, titled
`Verify in production: <the change, in a few words>`, its body the whole brief: the run that
verifies will never see this conversation and may be days away. **Every field a run reads is one
block on the first lines of the description**, ahead of your prose — the same placement
[`/do-later`](../do-later/SKILL.md) files under, and what gives the retry below one place to
rewrite `Not-before:`. Then say what changed and why it could not be watched now.

### The coded form — for a URL-readable artifact

```
Original-issue: #<the change's issue>
Task: claudinite-tasks/verify-production
Live-probe: <url> :: <assertion that becomes true when the release lands>
Verify-probe: <url> :: <the assertion being verified>
Retry-every: <how often to re-probe while not yet live, e.g. 6 hours>
```

The probes are the whole check, executed in code by the task the `Task:` line names —
no session, no `Model:`. `Live-probe:` is `In-production-when:` made executable and
`Verify-probe:` is `Verify:`; both classes are required, repeat either line for more
probes, and the assertion grammar (`status`, `contains`, `matches`, the `json` value
ops) is documented at its one home,
[`probes.mjs`](../../../claudinite-tasks/tasks/verify-production/probes.mjs). A
liveness probe failing re-arms the item by `Retry-every:`; a verify probe failing
against a live release reopens `Original-issue:` with what was asserted and what was
read; all passing closes the item with that evidence. No `Not-before:` is needed: a
coded run costs seconds, so probing from the moment of filing is the point, not a
waste — see the watch-it-fail step below.

### The agentic form — for a GitHub read

```
Original-issue: #<the change's issue>
In-production-when: <the concrete artifact to read, and what makes it true>
Verify: <what to observe, and what counts as a pass>
Not-before: <ISO instant just past the expected release>
Retry-every: <how far to push Not-before when not yet live, e.g. 1 day>
Model: sonnet
```

In either form, no `Blocked-by:`. You are filing after the merge, so the change's PR has
already closed and there is nothing left to wait on but the release itself.

- **`Original-issue:`** is where a failure lands — the issue the change was done under, which
  the run reopens if the verification fails. Make the verification that issue's **sub-issue**
  too (`mcp__github__sub_issue_write`, method `add`, `issue_number` the original,
  `sub_issue_id` the **id** the create call returned, not its number), so the change it proves
  shows what is still unproven about it — [RULES.md](../../RULES.md)' *Filing an issue that
  belongs under another*, applied where there is no PR left to carry the link.
- **`In-production-when:`** names a thing to *read*, never a duration to wait.
  "`missingbulb/Shepherd`'s `.claudinite-settings.json` stamps `packVersions.tidy-repo` at 8 or
  higher." "Any session started after this
  landed — check the vendored copy under `.claudinite/shared/` carries the new text." A merge
  is not a production condition, neither is elapsed time, and neither is anything the run
  cannot read.
- **`Verify:`** is an assertion with a pass condition, not a topic — and a read the run can
  actually make (the gate above): a file's content, an issue's state, a run's conclusion.
  "Issue #100 on that repo is closed with a comment citing the scheduler runs" beats "check
  tidy-issues works". A `Verify:` naming a person's step does not belong in this form at all —
  that is the rare human step above, an ordinary issue that never carries the mark.
- **`Not-before:`** is the queue's own wait field: adoption holds the run until the moment has
  passed. Aim it just past the release you expect — the re-arm covers a miss, so don't pad it.
- **`Retry-every:`** is the extension you are prescribing: when the run finds the change not
  yet live, it re-arms `Not-before:` to **now + `Retry-every:`** — never the old value plus it.
  Size it to the release you wait on — a nightly converge retries daily, a next-session rule in
  minutes.

Then the mark, as `/do-later` applies it: **`task:origin:ad-hoc`**, the one label the scheduler
run adopts — both forms alike. The agentic form's `Model: sonnet` is in its block because that
is the work: reading a live artifact and judging an assertion against it; the coded form names
no model, because nothing runs but code. Never `Automerge:` — a verification has nothing to
merge. If the mark doesn't exist in the repo yet, say so and leave the issue — it appears on the
next scheduler run.

## Tell the agentic run how to converge

The coded form needs none of this: its verdicts — requeue, pass, reopen — are the machinery's,
so its body ends with your prose and the playbook below would only be read as instructions by
something that takes none.

For the agentic form, end the body with instructions to the run itself — the issue is its whole
brief, and the run decides nothing: it executes this playbook.

**The transition off this issue is `converge-item.mjs`** — the command your instructions'
converge step names — **and never your own hand.** It reaches no network and needs none: it
reads the item you hand it, plans every side effect, and prints the calls for your own GitHub
tools to make. A session with no route to `api.github.com` runs it exactly like any other;
that is what it is for, so there is nothing here to improvise. **Never write a
`task:status:*` label by hand**: a hand-set `task:status:done` on an issue left open is a pass
recorded nowhere the queue reads, and the done label then hides the item from the leash, so
nothing ever comes back for it. (5)
If the command refuses, it is telling you this item is not yours to converge — say so and stop.

1. Read `In-production-when:` against the real artifact. Never infer it from a merge, a green
   run, or elapsed time. If it turns out you cannot read it at all from here, that is
   `--outcome action`, naming the read and who can make it — not a silent walk-away.
2. **Live** → run `Verify:`. Passes: converge `--outcome done`, its `--summary` carrying the
   evidence actually read (the version, the value, the path); the command closes this issue.
   Fails: reopen `Original-issue:` with a comment saying what was asserted, what happened
   instead and where you read it, then converge `--outcome done`, its summary linking that
   comment — the verification did its job by finding the fault, and the fault is now that
   issue's.
3. **Not yet live** → the one branch that converges nothing, because the run is not over: set
   `Not-before:` to **now + `Retry-every:`** — the instant you are
   reading this at, never the old value the field carries — **clear the issue's
   `task:status:*` label** (clearing the status is the whole of the re-ask — the mark stays on
   for life), and leave the issue open. The next scheduler run re-adopts it, and the bumped
   field holds it until the new moment. No comment; the bumped field is the record.

   Measure from the instant you read, because the queue releases a sleeping item on the
   first hourly pass past its moment, so by the time a run reads the field it is already
   behind — old + `Retry-every: 1 day` lands in the past again, the item goes ready on the
   very next pass, and a daily retry spends a session an hour. (6)

## Then watch it fail, and say what you filed

A coded verification runs for seconds, so its first execution is not left to faith: dispatch
the scheduler workflow (its `workflow_dispatch`) and
watch the first run report **not yet live** — proof the probes execute and fail for the right
reason instead of passing vacuously;
the same item then flips on its own once the release lands. A first run that *passes* before
the release you expected deserves a hard look, because a probe that cannot fail proves
nothing. The agentic form sleeps until its `Not-before:` and has no cheap forced run; filing
it correctly is the watch.

One line back to the owner: the issue link, what it waits on, and its retry cadence.
